about.title: Baldwin Park Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical care in Baldwin Park spans clinics, urgent care, outpatient surgery, and the larger hospital systems that serve this part of Los Angeles County. For most of the city's 77,071 residents, that care goes as planned. When it doesn't—when a diagnosis is missed, a medication is mixed up, or a surgical step is skipped—the aftermath can be confusing and expensive. California treats these cases under MICRA, a set of rules that differ from an ordinary injury claim. The clock is short: generally one year from when you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. Before filing, a 90-day notice must go to each provider. Nearly every case also needs a qualified medical expert to explain what the standard of care required and how it was breached. A poor result by itself is not enough. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Baldwin Park residents with an independent attorney who handles malpractice on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.desc: You generally have one year from discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury. An attorney in our network can evaluate where your timeline stands before it becomes a problem.

items.question: I was treated after a collision on the I-10 near Baldwin Park and the ER missed my injury. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but only if the provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that failure caused additional harm. Emergency medicine has its own standards, and a missed finding is not always negligence. A qualified medical expert would need to review your records to say whether the care met the standard. An attorney can arrange that review and also look at the separate crash claim.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Under MICRA, the deadline is generally one year from when you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and never more than three years from the date the injury occurred. A 90-day notice to each provider must be sent before a lawsuit is filed. Because these dates can be tricky to calculate, it helps to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages—things like pain and loss of enjoyment of life—under MICRA, and that cap rises each year. Economic losses such as medical bills and lost wages are not subject to the same cap. An attorney can explain how the current limits apply to your situation without promising any particular result.
